threat-model.title: Start with the failure
threat-model.caption: Examples to rank for your own circumstances; each control leaves dependencies.

nodes.title: Data lost
nodes.body: A damaged drive → separate current backups. Still depends on readable media and recovery credentials.

nodes.title: Unauthorized spend
nodes.body: A compromised online computer → offline signing and output review. Still depends on the signer and your checks.

nodes.title: Recovery knowledge lost
nodes.body: Someone else must recover → a rehearsed guide. Still depends on their access to the required material.

trust-test.title: One test, a specific conclusion
trust-test.caption: A restore-and-sign test proves a recovery path worked then. It cannot establish protection against every future threat.

nodes.title: Assumption
nodes.body: “This backup will work.”

nodes.title: Experiment
nodes.body: Restore a separate copy and sign a test payment.

nodes.title: Evidence and limit
nodes.body: Recovery worked; future theft resistance remains a separate question.

copies-authority.title: Copies preserve access. Policies assign authority.
copies-authority.caption: A copy of key A is still key A. Independent keys are not fragments of one secret.

nodes.title: Single-sig: A · A · A
nodes.body: Separate encrypted copies of the same signing authority. Any recovered copy can sign. Maintain locations, credentials and freshness.

nodes.title: 2-of-3: A + B, A + C, or B + C
nodes.body: Three distinct key identities; any two must sign. Maintain each signer AND the complete policy.

core-roles.title: Two jobs inside Bitcoin Core
core-roles.caption: The roles can run together or on separate computers. A wallet can sign only when it has the required private keys.

nodes.title: Node
nodes.body: Checks blocks and transactions against consensus rules.

nodes.title: Wallet
nodes.body: Recognizes its outputs, tracks payments and, with keys, signs.

ibd.title: Two activities can progress together
ibd.caption: Wait for synchronization before the course’s receive/send exercise; empty-wallet practice can proceed meanwhile.

several-signers.title: One verified chain, separate signing devices
several-signers.caption: PSBT files are individual transfers, not permanent network links. This arrangement alone does not define a multisig policy.

nodes.title: Online node
nodes.body: Validates history and coordinates proposals.

nodes.title: Offline signer A
nodes.body: Receives a PSBT file, reviews and signs with its own keys.

nodes.title: Offline signer B
nodes.body: Receives a separate PSBT file; no blockchain download required.

backup-models.title: Root material and a wallet snapshot
backup-models.caption: Both models require a tested recovery procedure. Neither is a complete custody system by itself.
rows: Words encode entropy and a checksum; a seed is derived using the optional BIP39 passphrase.
Any BIP39 passphrase; required paths, script types, policies and instructions.
Key material, descriptors and wallet metadata as of the backup.
Encryption passphrase and recovery instructions; current policy information.

entropy.title: Randomness creates secret material
entropy.caption: Conceptual metaphor, not the exact RNG algorithm. Operating-system randomness is a principal input; extra inputs do not justify adding arbitrary entropy totals.
entropy.alt: A dominant blue input enters a simple mixing chamber beside a laptop; an abstract gold pattern represents newly generated secret material.

generation-encryption.title: Generation and encryption do different jobs
generation-encryption.caption: The wallet passphrase protects existing secret material. It is not the source of the Bitcoin signing keys.

nodes.title: Generate
nodes.body: Core’s random-number system supplies material for wallet secrets.

nodes.title: Encrypt
nodes.body: The wallet passphrase protects access to private key material in the file.

checksum-randomness.title: A format check cannot measure unpredictability
checksum-randomness.caption: A valid checksum answers a formatting question. The generation method must supply the randomness.

nodes.title: Checksum: format
nodes.body: Does this representation satisfy its checksum rule?

nodes.title: Randomness: generation
nodes.body: Could an attacker predict how the secret was chosen? A checksum cannot answer.

continuity.title: Recovery is maintained across replacements
continuity.caption: Keep instructions usable, backups readable and recovery tested as hardware and software change. No particular program or vendor is guaranteed to last for decades.
continuity.alt: Three generations of ordinary computers, each with maintained notes and backup media; a person tests the replacement.

ai-review.title: Turn a suggestion into a checked experiment
ai-review.caption: If the observed result differs, stop and investigate the mismatch before trying more commands.

nodes.title: Explain
nodes.body: What changes? Which files and permissions are involved?

nodes.title: Verify
nodes.body: Compare the proposal with the project’s documentation.

nodes.title: Test
nodes.body: Use disposable data and a harmless, reversible task.

nodes.title: Observe
nodes.body: Compare the result with the expected behavior.

software-review.title: Review what you let run
software-review.caption: A signed repository helps establish origin and integrity. It does not prove every package harmless.

nodes.title: Source
nodes.body: Where did this program come from?

nodes.title: Maintainer
nodes.body: Who maintains and updates it?

nodes.title: Permissions
nodes.body: What can it read or change?

nodes.title: Need
nodes.body: Does this dedicated computer need it?

clean-start.title: Carry forward understanding
clean-start.caption: Keep reviewed notes and required verified files. Reinstall the operating system for the dedicated setup; do not clone the experimental system. Reinstallation does not repair compromised firmware.
clean-start.alt: Two separate worktables: an experimental laptop and a clean dedicated laptop. Only a notebook of understood instructions crosses between them.

verification.title: Three checks, three different questions
verification.caption: Builder signing keys are not wallet keys. A matching hash and signature do not replace code review.
states: Current check: compare the downloaded archive with its listed SHA256 digest.
Current check: verify signatures over the listed checksums.
Current check: independently confirm the builder-key fingerprints.

builds.title: Independent builders compare artifacts
builds.caption: Matching builds connect artifacts to a defined source and build process. They do not prove the source free of vulnerabilities.

nodes.title: Same source + build conditions
nodes.body: Pinned inputs and an agreed build procedure.

nodes.title: Independent builders
nodes.body: Each produces and attests to its artifacts.

nodes.title: Compare results
nodes.body: Matching outputs provide reproducibility evidence.

networks.title: Separate networks, separate practice
networks.caption: Check the chain field in Core. Test coins do not turn into mainnet bitcoin.

nodes.title: Signet
nodes.body: chain: signet • test history and test-wallet context.

nodes.title: Mainnet
nodes.body: chain: main • real bitcoin and a new wallet setup.

pruning.title: Validation first; storage choice second
pruning.caption: Both validate the chain. A rescan needs the relevant historical blocks; pruning can require downloading missing history again.

separate-credentials.title: Recovery needs both, kept separately
separate-credentials.caption: If credentials are in a password-manager database, plan recovery of that database too. Avoid circular dependencies.

nodes.title: Backup location
nodes.body: Encrypted wallet backup. Protect availability and confidentiality.

nodes.title: Separate credential location
nodes.body: Recoverable passphrase record. Do not store only beside the backup.

nodes.title: Recovery procedure
nodes.body: Bring both to the intended recovery device when needed.

first-encryption.title: First encryption requires a fresh backup
first-encryption.caption: The old file is not encrypted retroactively. Core 31.1 creates fresh active descriptors on first encryption; preserve the post-encryption state using Core’s backup function.

nodes.title: Before
nodes.body: An old unencrypted snapshot remains an old unencrypted file.

nodes.title: Encrypt current wallet
nodes.body: Private key material is protected; active descriptors are refreshed.

nodes.title: After
nodes.body: Create and test a new encrypted backup.

transaction.title: Follow every output
transaction.caption: Illustrative test transaction in satoshis. Both payment and change belong to you in this self-transfer exercise. The fee is the difference, not an output.

coin-linkage.title: Combining inputs can link their histories
coin-linkage.caption: Observers may infer common ownership. Fee depends on transaction size and feerate, not simply on the BTC value transferred.

nodes.title: Input A
nodes.body: Previously separate history.

nodes.title: Input B
nodes.body: Another previously separate history.

nodes.title: One transaction
nodes.body: Both are spent together; their relationship becomes visible.

restore.title: Restore into a separate wallet
restore.caption: Keep the original closed. After any required rescan, compare known addresses and transactions; the next exercise proves signing.

nodes.title: Original wallet
nodes.body: Close it; preserve it outside this recovery test.

nodes.title: Backup snapshot
nodes.body: Restore through Core under a new name.

nodes.title: Restored wallet
nodes.body: Check history and then prove it can sign.

old-backup.title: A password change does not rewrite copies
old-backup.caption: Both snapshots retain the same Bitcoin signing authority. A new passphrase neither revokes a copied key nor changes the password on an old file.

lifecycle.title: Repeat the complete cycle
lifecycle.caption: Repeat in separate sessions with disposable wallets. This map records no completion and introduces no additional required clicks.

nodes.title: 1 · Create and protect
nodes.body: Create → encrypt → backup.

nodes.title: 2 · Use
nodes.body: Receive → review → send.

nodes.title: 3 · Recover
nodes.body: Restore → sign a test transaction.

nodes.title: 4 · Change and retest
nodes.body: Change passphrase → new backup → restore and sign again.

wallet-node-data.title: Different data, different recovery
wallet-node-data.caption: Bitcoin is recorded by the network, not stored as coins in wallet.dat. Make wallet backups through Core; do not copy an open database.

nodes.title: blocks/
nodes.body: Public block history. Can be downloaded again.

nodes.title: chainstate/
nodes.body: Validation state derived from block history. Can be rebuilt.

nodes.title: wallets/…/wallet.dat
nodes.body: Wallet keys, descriptors and metadata. Preserve a tested backup.

backup-matrix.title: Independence and freshness are separate axes
backup-matrix.caption: An old snapshot may miss a required change; receiving each new payment does not automatically require a backup. Keep the passphrase record separately.
rows: May lose both access and needed changes
Current, but one event can destroy all copies
Survives local loss, may miss needed changes
Independent current copy — still test recovery

encryption-boundary.title: What Core wallet encryption protects
encryption-boundary.caption: Encryption protects private key material. Public keys, addresses, labels and history may remain readable; an external container adds a separate credential and recovery dependency.

architecture.title: Online coordination · offline signing
architecture.caption: Private signing keys stay offline. Review every transfer and verify payment details on the signer.

wallet-roles.title: Connection and signing authority are different properties
wallet-roles.caption: Watch-only information can expose financial activity. “Offline” describes the device’s network state, not a special kind of key.

media-roles.title: Give each medium one role
media-roles.caption: Transfer files are untrusted input to review. A transfer drive must not double as a private wallet backup or credential record.

nodes.title: Transfer medium
nodes.body: Public descriptors and PSBT files only.

nodes.title: Private backup medium
nodes.body: Encrypted wallet backup; kept outside transfer workflow.

nodes.title: Credential record
nodes.body: Passphrase, recoverable separately.

tamper-response.title: A credible concern changes the recovery path
tamper-response.caption: Being left unattended is not itself proof of compromise. Follow the stop conditions in your threat model.

nodes.title: Stop
nodes.body: Take the suspect signer out of service.

nodes.title: Replace
nodes.body: Prepare a trusted replacement and recover offline.

nodes.title: If keys may be copied
nodes.body: Generate new keys and verify a transfer to the new wallet. Replacing hardware alone cannot revoke old keys.

offline-preparation.title: Finish setup before secrets exist
offline-preparation.caption: Disconnect before creating or restoring keys. A successful cold boot checks persistence; it is not an independent backup recovery test.

nodes.title: Preparation · no secrets
nodes.body: Install and verify the OS and Core; finish downloads.

nodes.title: Disconnect boundary
nodes.body: Disable networking before introducing wallet secrets.

nodes.title: Offline use
nodes.body: Create or restore; back up; cold-boot and check. Do not return this signer to downloading software.

descriptors.title: Public descriptions cross; signing keys stay
descriptors.caption: Both receive and change branches let the coordinator recognize the same outputs. Public descriptors grant no signature authority, but can reveal financial activity.

import-metadata.title: Descriptor expression ≠ import options
import-metadata.caption: Schematic field guide only. Use the actual test descriptor and values from the lesson; do not import this illustration.
rows: The output descriptor expression, with its checksum.
Derivation range and the next address index.
Whether this descriptor supplies new addresses.

psbt-flow.title: The same payment, different states
psbt-flow.caption: Saving is not signing; signing is not broadcasting. Core’s GUI may combine finalization and extraction with the final broadcast action.
states: Current step: prepare and save the unsigned PSBT online.
Current step: review every proposed output on the offline signer.
Current step: sign and save on the offline device.
Current step: return the PSBT online, finalize, extract and broadcast.

recovery-both.title: Recover without either original
recovery-both.caption: Bring the private backup and its separate credential only to the replacement offline signer. The replacement online coordinator receives public descriptors.
states: Current step: restore the replacement offline signer.
Current step: rebuild the replacement watch-only coordinator.
Current step: prove a confirmed payment using only the replacements.

handover.title: Can another person follow the guide?
handover.caption: Rehearse with a disposable wallet while the author observes without hidden instructions. Access to recovery material and legal ownership are separate questions.
handover.alt: A learner follows a written guide on a replacement laptop while the author observes silently; backup media and the credential record are handled separately.

container.title: Two encryption layers, two recovery stages
container.caption: Keep container recovery instructions and required header-recovery material available. Do not put the only credential record inside the container it unlocks.

nodes.title: Outer container
nodes.body: VeraCrypt credential opens the container.

nodes.title: Core backup inside
nodes.body: Extract the already encrypted wallet backup.

nodes.title: Wallet unlock
nodes.body: The Core wallet passphrase unlocks its private key material.

migration.title: Reuse block files; rebuild derived state
migration.caption: Use your own complete archive, with Core shut down. Pruned history has gaps and is not enough for a full local rebuild. Wallets and configuration follow separate procedures.

nodes.title: Source blocks/
nodes.body: Copy the whole directory, including xor.dat when present.

nodes.title: Replacement node
nodes.body: Rebuild block index and chainstate from those block files.

tails-storage.title: Session, persistent storage, independent backup
tails-storage.caption: Persistent Storage uses its own credential; the Core wallet has a separate passphrase. Tails does not repair compromised hardware or firmware.

nodes.title: Live session
nodes.body: Temporary data disappears on shutdown.

nodes.title: Persistent Storage
nodes.body: Only selected persistent data survives, on this USB device.

nodes.title: Independent backup
nodes.body: Core backup on a separate medium, with tested recovery. Persistence alone is not a backup.

tails-storage.boundary: The same underlying hardware and firmware

lab-host.title: Two processes, one physical host
lab-host.caption: A disposable Regtest lab demonstrates software roles. It does not create physical isolation or an air gap.

nodes.title: Node process
nodes.body: Temporary node directory; networkactive=false.

nodes.title: Signer process
nodes.body: Separate temporary wallet directory; still the same host.

lab-host.boundary: One physical computer · shared OS and hardware

descriptor-policy.title: wsh(sortedmulti(2,A,B,C))
descriptor-policy.caption: Schematic notation, not an executable descriptor. A, B and C stand for complete key expressions; real values and checksum come from the lab.
rows: Any two designated keys; public keys sorted in the script.
Three independent key identities, not pieces of one key.
timestamp, range and active are outside the descriptor string.

psbt-states.title: Signatures are only one part of the process
psbt-states.caption: The combiner merges information for the same unsigned transaction. A finalized or broadcast transaction is not yet a block confirmation.

nodes.title: Unsigned / partial
nodes.body: Input data and zero or some required signatures.

nodes.title: Enough signatures
nodes.body: Each input has the required signing contributions.

nodes.title: Finalize and extract
nodes.body: Build scriptSig/witness, then extract the raw transaction.

nodes.title: Broadcast
nodes.body: Submit to the node; acceptance and confirmation remain separate.

combine.title: Independent signatures, one transaction
combine.caption: A and B each sign the same original proposal. C is an alternative signer, not a required third signature. Never combine different transactions.

policy-backup.title: Recovery needs keys AND the complete policy
policy-backup.caption: The public policy is privacy-sensitive: preserve it, do not publish it. Keep each signer’s private contribution protected separately.

nodes.title: Complete public policy
nodes.body: All required public keys, derivation information and script structure.

nodes.title: Private contributions
nodes.body: Enough recovered independent signers to meet the threshold.

nodes.title: Recovery proof
nodes.body: Derive matching outputs, sign and verify the intended spend.

quorum-tests.title: Predict the 2-of-3 result, then test
quorum-tests.caption: Observed results belong in your own lab record and remain unfilled here. These expectations assume the complete correct policy and transaction.

taproot.title: Alternative paths, not automatic quorum
taproot.caption: Adding a threshold script does not remove key-path authority. A plain tr(KEY) in this lab is a key-path single-sig example.

relative-delay.title: The output starts its own clock
relative-delay.caption: Regtest wsh example: ordinary 2-of-3 OR recovery child key C with older(6). A signature can exist before the delay is satisfied; transaction version and sequence must also be correct.

path-tests.title: Test the policy actually constructed
path-tests.caption: The delayed wsh experiment and the plain Taproot key-path experiment are separate. This does not claim arbitrary Taproot script trees have been tested.
